F1: A ProximityPrompt only works when its parent is a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model (it uses the PrimaryPart). A Folder has no position, so the prompt never shows. In a Model with no PrimaryPart it also has nothing to anchor to. Fix: parent it to a part (or an Attachment in a part) at the counter. If it only shows from some angles, RequiresLineOfSight (default true) is being blocked by the stand's own geometry or a hitbox. Set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or move the part/Attachment so it sits in front of the geometry. Also check: Enabled = true, MaxActivationDistance is large enough, the prompt's position is in front of the stand (raise UIOffset if needed), Style is Default (Custom style draws nothing unless you build the UI), ClickablePrompt, and that ProximityPromptService.Enabled is on and no script hides prompts.
F2: 1) Ownership. Animations only load in games owned by the same user/group that owns the animation asset. Re-upload (or publish) the animation under the group, or grant the group's experience permission, and use the new ID. In Studio, your own account's animations work, which is why it plays there. 2) Use Humanoid.Animator:LoadAnimation (Humanoid:LoadAnimation is deprecated). Load it from the client on the local character's Animator, which replicates. Wait for the Animator: char:WaitForChild('Humanoid'):WaitForChild('Animator'). Cache the track instead of reloading it on every swing. 3) Half-blending: set track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action (or Action2-4) so it overrides Walk/Run/Idle, or set Priority on the asset in the Animation Editor before export. Also make sure the animation keys every arm joint you want overridden, because unkeyed joints keep playing the walk. Check that the weight is 1 (track:Play(0.1, 1, 1)). Make sure the rig type (R6 vs R15) matches the animation.
F3: LayoutOrder is only used when UIListLayout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder. The default for older layouts, or one set to Name, sorts alphabetically by Name, so set SortOrder to LayoutOrder. LayoutOrder is an integer, so prices fit. Ties: when two siblings have the same LayoutOrder, the order is not defined by a secondary key you control. It depends on internal child order, which can change when instances are re-parented, cloned or replicated, so they can appear to swap. Fix: give each item a unique LayoutOrder, for example price*10 + index, or break ties by encoding a secondary key.
F4:
local MPS = game:GetService('MarketplaceService')
local DSS = game:GetService('DataStoreService')
local receipts = DSS:GetDataStore('PurchaseHistory')
local PRODUCT = 123456

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local player = game.Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  if info.ProductId ~= PRODUCT then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local key = info.PlayerId .. '_' .. info.PurchaseId
  local ok, err = pcall(function()
    receipts:UpdateAsync(key, function(done)
      if done then return nil end -- already granted
      addCoins(player, 100) -- your data module; must be saved/persisted
      return true
    end)
  end)
  if not ok then warn(err) return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end

Rules: set ProcessReceipt exactly once, in one server Script. Never grant from the client or from PromptProductPurchaseFinished. Make it idempotent by PurchaseId. Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. Otherwise return NotProcessedYet and Roblox retries. Never yield forever or error. pcall DataStore calls. Handle the player having left. Ideally the session-locked profile records PurchaseIds and is saved before you return.
F5:
local CAS = game:GetService('ContextActionService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

local function setSpeed(s)
  local hum = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if hum then hum.WalkSpeed = s end
end

local function sprint(_, state, _)
  if state == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then setSpeed(24)
  elseif state == Enum.UserInputState.End or state == Enum.UserInputState.Cancel then setSpeed(16) end
  return Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass
end

CAS:BindAction('Sprint', sprint, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3)
CAS:SetTitle('Sprint', 'Run')
CAS:SetPosition('Sprint', UDim2.new(1, -150, 1, -150))
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function() setSpeed(16) end)

Rules: put it in StarterPlayerScripts (or StarterCharacterScripts). The third argument true creates the touch button, which is shown only on touch devices. Handle End and Cancel, since Cancel fires when focus is lost or the action is unbound, so you never get stuck sprinting. Return Pass or Sink as appropriate. Unbind with CAS:UnbindAction when needed. WalkSpeed set on the client replicates for your own character, so the server should validate speed for anti-cheat.
F6:
local hinge = door.HingeConstraint -- Attachment0 on frame, Attachment1 on door; the hinge axis is the attachments' X axis (point it vertically)
hinge.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
hinge.LimitsEnabled = true
hinge.LowerAngle = 0
hinge.UpperAngle = 90
hinge.AngularSpeed = 2 -- rad/s
hinge.ServoMaxTorque = 1e6

local open = false
prompt.Triggered:Connect(function()
  open = not open
  hinge.TargetAngle = open and 90 or 0
end)

The properties that matter: ActuatorType = Servo, which drives to TargetAngle in degrees. AngularSpeed sets the swing speed, and ServoMaxTorque must be high enough to move the door's mass. AngularResponsiveness also matters for stiffness. Turn on LimitsEnabled with LowerAngle/UpperAngle (and Restitution) to clamp the swing. Attachment orientation sets the axis, so the attachment's primary axis must be vertical at the hinge edge. The door must be unanchored. The frame should be anchored. The door should not collide with the frame (use a NoCollisionConstraint or collision groups). For server-authoritative motion, keep network ownership on the server: door:SetNetworkOwner(nil). Use a light part or Massless pieces so the torque suffices.
F7: Use MessagingService. An admin client fires a RemoteEvent with the text. The server verifies the sender is an admin (a UserId or group-rank check on the server, never trusting the client), rate-limits, filters the text with TextService:FilterStringAsync and GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync, then calls MessagingService:PublishAsync('Announce', {text=..., id=..., t=os.time()}) inside a pcall with retry. Every server calls SubscribeAsync('Announce', fn) at startup (in a pcall). The handler fires a RemoteEvent with FireAllClients to show the banner. The publishing server also receives its own message, so don't show it twice. Limits: the message payload is about 1 KB. Publish throughput is about 150 + 60*players per minute per server, and subscriptions are limited per server. Delivery is best-effort with no guarantee and no ordering, typically under a second. Delivery is not persisted, so servers started later miss it. For a 'current announcement' that new servers need, also store it in a DataStore or MemoryStore with an expiry and read it on startup. Dedupe by id. Keep topic names short. It does not work across experiences.
F8: Client: play the swing animation and sound immediately, with optional local hit VFX for feel. Fire a RemoteEvent ('Swing'), or let the server detect hits on its own. Server: own all damage. On Swing, check the tool is equipped by that player, the character is alive, and the cooldown (server-side timestamp per player). Do the hit detection on the server (GetPartBoundsInBox / a Shapecast / spatial query in front of the HumanoidRootPart, or Touched on the blade during an active window), or validate a client-reported target. The target must be within range (distance plus ping slack), alive, not on the same team, and hit at most once per swing. Apply Humanoid:TakeDamage on the server. Never accept a damage amount from the client. Equip issue: by default Tool.RequiresHandle = true, so it needs a part named exactly 'Handle'. Rename 'Blade' to 'Handle' (or add a Handle part and weld the Blade to it with a WeldConstraint). Make it unanchored with CanCollide off, and adjust the grip with Tool.Grip / GripPos. Otherwise set RequiresHandle = false.
F9: UnreliableRemoteEvent suits frequent, ephemeral, superseded data where a lost or out-of-order packet doesn't matter because the next update replaces it: aim direction, cursor, cosmetic look-at, VFX triggers. Constraints: delivery is not guaranteed and ordering is not guaranteed. The payload is limited (about 1000 bytes per call). Larger payloads are dropped, not sent. There's no ack. Don't use it for game-critical events (damage, purchases, state changes) or one-off events. It uses the same API (FireServer/FireAllClients/OnClientEvent) and the same security rules (validate and rate-limit on the server). Also reduce the cost: send compact data (a quantized yaw/pitch number instead of a CFrame), send only when it changed beyond a threshold, use a lower rate (10-20 Hz), and interpolate on receivers. Batch players into one server broadcast per tick instead of relaying each one. Consider skipping players far away.
F10: 1) With streaming, parts far from the player may not exist on the client yet. Use workspace:WaitForChild('Map'):WaitForChild('Castle'):WaitForChild('Gate') (with a timeout), or listen with ChildAdded / CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal and handle removal (streaming out). Mark the Castle model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so it streams as a unit, or Persistent/PersistentPerPlayer if the client must always have it. Never assume a streamed instance stays. 2) Teleport void: the destination area isn't streamed in when you move the character. On the server, call player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(targetPosition, timeout) before setting the character CFrame (pivot), or on the client before moving. Also consider anchoring the HumanoidRootPart briefly until the floor exists. Tune StreamingMinRadius / StreamingTargetRadius. Use StreamingIntegrityMode (PauseOutsideLoadedArea) so the player is paused rather than falling.
F11: Roblox shipped Luau's new type solver (a rewrite of the type inference engine) out of beta in Studio. It was previously opt-in via the Beta Features 'New Luau type solver'. Changes: better inference (generalization, type functions such as keyof/index/user-defined 'type function's, read-only properties, improved refinements and unions/intersections, fewer false positives). Script Analysis and autocomplete use it. --!strict, --!nonstrict and --!nocheck mode comments still work the same way; the solver choice is a separate setting. To enable it: in Studio, File > Beta Features (or Studio Settings > Script Editor/Luau, depending on version) enable 'New Luau Type Solver' and restart Studio. It then applies to all scripts, including --!strict ones. Outside Studio (luau-lsp / luau-analyze), enable the new solver flag (e.g. luau-lsp 'luau-lsp.fflags.enableNewSolver' / FFlag LuauSolverV2=true). Expect some new errors in strict code. Fix annotations rather than downgrading to nonstrict.
F12:
The Input Action System is Roblox's declarative, instance-based input layer, replacing much of ContextActionService/UserInputService binding code. Instances: InputContext (a group of actions with Enabled, Priority, Sink; put it under a player's PlayerGui/client), InputAction (one action with Type = Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition etc.; events Pressed, Released, StateChanged; GetState()), and InputBinding (a child of an InputAction mapping a source: KeyCode, a composite Up/Down/Left/Right for directions, or UIButton = a GuiButton for touch). Example (LocalScript):
local ctx = Instance.new('InputContext')
ctx.Parent = player.PlayerGui
local jump = Instance.new('InputAction')
jump.Name = 'Jump'; jump.Type = Enum.InputActionType.Bool; jump.Parent = ctx
local kb = Instance.new('InputBinding'); kb.KeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.Space; kb.Parent = jump
local btn = Instance.new('InputBinding'); btn.UIButton = screenGui.JumpButton; btn.Parent = jump
jump.Pressed:Connect(function()
  local hum = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if hum then hum.Jump = true end
end)
You can also build these in Explorer, without code. Use context Priority/Sink to override default controls.
